_note: M0-TH's manifest. One scope per thing checkable today; each lot that builds a §5 surface adds its scopes (docs/agent/testing.md). Plants: tests/plants/<plant>.patch, or a command for a plant on a file that moves (plan_lint).

plan_lint.desc: the plan's structure: every block, Flow row, status word, budget (plan.py lint)

plants.patch: {python} -S -c "import pathlib;p=pathlib.Path('milestones/m0/m0_implementation_plan.md');t=p.read_text(encoding='utf-8');assert '- Status: DONE' in t;p.write_text(t.replace('- Status: DONE','- Status: WIBBLE',1),encoding='utf-8')"

tools_selftest.desc: each annex tool's own red-armed selftest - proves the tools, never the game

toolchain.desc: the picked stack builds a one-file program: desktop (rustc 1.99), wasm32, and the web page through trunk 0.21.14 - not the game's GO

build.desc: the game's workspace builds and lints clean natively (cargo build + clippy -D warnings, release) and checks for wasm32-unknown-unknown (M0-T1)

registry.desc: the element, constant and reaction registries and the sandbox units (contract §1.5, §1.6, §2.1, §2.5.1, §2.7): elements.json's ten species verbatim and in order, physics.json's constants at their initial values, every bound at its edge (the ignition ladder, T_Si/T_H, Σ_N, ν, f_dep, κ_dust, the K pairs), each refusal naming its key, 1/μ, Y_e and Z_met of the solar mix against hand values, M0 = 2πΣc a²/3 (M0-T10); reactions.json's ten records verbatim, shares summing to 1 within 1e-12, keys resolving, ν ≥ 4, stand-ins disabled, each refusal naming its record (M0-T11)

eos.desc: the equation of state (contract §2.3.1-§2.3.3, §2.7): Π_th = Σε_th and T = με_th, the cold pressure P(x; K₁, K₂)'s two limits within 1e-6, u(x) = x∫P/s² tabulated on 512 log-spaced points over [1e-8, 1e8] and checked against the integral in closed form at the nodes, against both limits' closed forms, and between nodes within 1e-4 (the log-log interpolation), monotone, finite at the low end, K = 0 meaning no cold pressure, ε_th from E floored at T_floor/μ with the floor booked, c² = 2Π/Σ (M0-T12)

time_control.desc: time control, no GPU (contract §1.8, §3.2, §4.3, §4.12): the ladder and TOP / 1.5, the game at ×1 running, select/faster/slower at the ends, N = min(N_max, ⌈owed/Δt_est⌉) with owed booked from read-back frames and bounded to [−Δt_est, one frame], N_max from the 16-frame c_step average and R_reserve, the cap readout at 30 of the last 60 frames, 10,000 capped frames then ×0.1 with no backlog, pause and one step per press, the slow-down only ever slower with no auto-return, the latch's stopped steps never owed, the 30-frames switch at TOP (30 of 60, 120 quiet), the empty world's Δt survived, speed text at two significant digits (M0-T24)

strings.desc: the string table (contract §4.1, §5.4 G-STR): crates/sr-app/src/strings.rs and the contract's `strings` block hold the same keys, each way, with byte-identical texts (× — ≈ · … compared as bytes), and web/index.html carries each web.* text verbatim; the test includes strings.rs by #[path] because sr-app is bin-only (M0-T13)

adapter.desc: the GPU adapter choice (contract §6.1-§6.3, §6.2.2): the matching rule on a fixed list, and a live headless device per adapter this box has, at WebGPU's default limits (M0-T2); box's adapters named in the log

state.desc: the cell state and the step loop (contract §2.2, §2.8, §1.3.2, §1.3.4): WorldConfig's sizes, a 600 × 400 upload/readback round trip bit-exact, P0-P9's order, P8's species renormalisation (Σ X = 1 within 1e-6, other channels bit-identical), two runs bit-identical (M0-T3); on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

booking.desc: the side fields and the booking layout (contract §2.2, §1.9.1, §2.9, §1.3.4): every §2.9 booked term and §1.9.1 accumulator listed with its writer pass; a test pipeline books known values into every slot over 16 steps, each term's f64 total (book_totals) equal to the closed form within 1e-9 relative; two runs bit-identical; the clear empties every term (M0-T18); on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

floors.desc: P8 complete and the equation of state on the GPU (contract §1.3.2, §1.5, §2.3.2-§2.3.3, §2.7, §2.9): eos.wgsl's helpers (1/μ, Y_e, Z_met, Π_e, Π_n, ε_cold from M0-T12's u(x) table, Π, c², T) against sr_physics::eos with the cold pairs on and off; P8 lists floor_cells ahead of renormalise_species; a 64 × 64 field of vacuum, cold, dense cold and hot cells with normalised, unnormalised, mixed-sign and all-≤0 fractions → one step → vacuum cells at the floor state, cold cells at T_floor (2e-5 relative of the f64 twin), hot cells bit-identical, fractions renormalised (1e-6), vacuum_reset and floor_added equal to the mass and energy changed within 1e-6 relative, cell by cell and in total (M0-T19); cells holding a NaN or an Inf fraction left bit-identical for P9's guard, nothing booked, every other cell as the clean run (M0-D18); on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

dt.desc: P1 Δt, P9's Δt reduction and the non-finite guard (contract §1.3.2 P1 and P9, §1.3.4, §2.3.3, §2.3.5, §3.3): P1 holds dt_advance, P9 dt_cells and dt_partials, plus guard_scan and guard_stamp every 64th step; Δt against §2.3.5's formula in f64 (C = 0.4, η_g = 0.3, the gravity term infinite until P2) on fields of known u and c, the cold pairs off, 64 × 64, 72 × 88 and 600 × 400, within 1e-6 relative; step 0 on the initial state's reduction and step n on the value P9 made at the end of step n − 1; Δt and the state bit-identical over two 130-step runs on 600 × 400; a NaN and an Inf planted at known cells and steps → the guard's step, cell and channel (M0-T20); a NaN x_C planted before step 0 → named by step 0's scan, its cell's fractions as planted (M0-D18); on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

box.desc: the active box (contract §1.3.3, §1.3.2, §1.3.4; G-BOX's box half, its conservation cases with M0-T39): the bounding box of Σ ≥ Σ_vac cells grown by 8, rounded out to 8, clamped to the world — blobs in the middle, on and off the 8-grid, at each edge and corner, a block, two far corners, Σ = Σ_vac and the next f32 below, the empty world — exactly; the FFT size per axis (smallest power of two ≥ 2 × the box, at least 32; up to 4096 on a 2048-wide world); the re-fit after P9 at step indices ≡ 0 (mod 16) only, and in P0 when the edit flag is set (cleared by the fit); P8's two dispatches and dt_cells sized indirectly from the box's buffer, P8 leaving the vacuum outside the box as uploaded, Δt over the box against the f64 formula (1e-6); the whole-world switch (M0-T21); on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

latch.desc: a frame of steps and the collapse latch (contract §1.8.3, §1.8.5, §1.8.7, §3.1; G-LATCH's mechanism — its contract scenario arrives with M0-T111, until then NOT PROVEN (synthetic)): a test hook sets the flag in P6 at step k of a 40-step frame (k = 1, 15, 40; 15 puts the re-fit after step index 16 inside the stopped stretch) → exactly k steps run, the state, the Δt record and the box bit-identical to a k-step run, no box-sized dispatch after step k, the next frame whole; slow-down off → all 40; re-armed only after 1.0 t.u. without a set (Δt ≈ 0.447 checked first); P0's gate zeroed when an edit is flagged on the firing step; poll() reports each frame once, in order, without waiting (M0-T22); on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

timing.desc: GPU timestamps, the cost per step and headless --timing (contract §1.8.3's c_step, §2.12.2's timing, §3.1's poll(), §3.3, §6.2.2): with timing on, every pass a step records (P0 always, then each pass with a dispatch) is timed at its compute-pass boundaries, positive, no other pass named, their sum within 40 % of the step's cost (first pass's beginning to last pass's end; TW's submission-overhead note) — over bare steps (read_cost), frames (poll()'s FrameReport.cost, frame begin + end timed, two frames in flight each with its own steps) and a 1000-step frame that outgrows the 4096-query set (its first whole steps timed, the next frame fresh); the device holds no feature but timestamp-query, and that one only where the adapter offers it; the wall-clock fallback names itself and times no pass; timing off → no cost; headless --timing on the nominal disk (in-process, the function the binary forwards to) writes summary.json's timing with every recorded pass in per_pass_ms, step_ms_mean and source, and no timing key without the flag (M0-T23). A mechanism scope, not a ⏱ one: no speed is graded, so it runs on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

scene.desc: scene files (contract §2.12.1, §2.12.4, §2.10's cloud, §2.8's world and edge, §3.3's headless --scene --world --edge): an unknown key refused at every level (top, world, switches — the misspelt hydor — test, each object kind, composition), naming its path, and through headless as exit 4 with no summary; t with pressure refused, neither refused; overrides only physics.json keys, within physics.json's bounds, a scene with overrides never writing calibration; objects where §2.12.4 puts them (x right, y down, cell centres, rects clipped), overlapping objects adding, a resized world keeping them about its centre, an object off the world a warning; E from t and Π from pressure through the EOS, a pressure under the cold pressure refused; a disk's mass read back from the GPU against 2πΣc a²/3 within the outer ring's bound 2√2 a^-3/2; every file in scenes/ parsing, sun_disk.json the preset:sun planes bit for bit, fill_world.json filling every world shape; headless --scene scenes/sun_disk.json --world 256x256 --edge bounce --steps 5 writing summary.json's scene and world as given (M0-T25)

dump.desc: state dumps (contract §2.12.3 with §0.5 [M0-T26]'s resume key, §3.1's load_dump and dump_state, §3.3's --dump-every and --load-dump, §1.3.4): the bytes read by hand — SRDUMP01, the u32 header length, the header's eight keys (version, width, height, step, sim_time, channels in §2.2's order, sinks, resume), 14 little-endian f32 planes row-major, Σ, mom_x and mom_y found at §2.2's indices by the start's values — then read back to the same dump and the same bytes, through a file, and load_dump → dump_state bit for bit; 2 × 100 steps through a dump (frames under the latch, a fire on the dump's last step, a second flag 2 Δt later) equal 200 straight steps — the state, the Δt record, the box and every frame report — and the cells alone visibly do not; headless 100 + --load-dump 100 writes the 200-step run's s_150 and s_200 byte for byte, --dump-every 50 at step indices from the scene, the final dump always, a --world other than the dump's and --dump-every without --out exit 4; a dump cut anywhere, one byte too long, a wrong magic, an unknown or missing key, another version, world or channel list refused, naming it, and through headless exit 4 with no summary (M0-T26); one sim time per step count — 40 steps as 1 × 40, 2 × 20, 40 × 1 frames and bare give byte-identical dumps, the reports' sim time the dump's, within 1e-9 relative of the f64 sum of each step's f32 Δt in order (the f32 sum visibly not); an empty world's steps (Δt the largest f32) add none; headless --steps 100 writes summary.json's and the final dump's sim_time equal, its in-process twin's, within the bound (M0-D21); on the physics adapter (R12, R15)

boot.desc: the headless boot (contract §3.3, §3.4, §5.4 G-BOOT): launch.py smoke of headless-boot is ready within 60 s and its summary.json carries every §2.12.2 key with steps = 200; stdout opens with SR-ADAPTER and ends with SR-HEADLESS DONE steps=200 (M0-T4); the build is the tree's own

desktop.desc: the desktop boot (contract §3.3, §3.4, §3.6, §5.4 G-DESK): launch.py smoke of the box's window route — game-xvfb (private Xvfb, lavapipe) on linux-pc, game-offscreen on win-laptop (R15) — reads /status "ready" within 90 s, raised by the first presented frame (M0-T5), and the double-click launcher fed its Enter on the same route - starts, reaches ready, stops, leaves nothing running (M0-T6); the build is the tree's own

web.desc: G-WEB (contract §3.5, §6.2.1, §6.2.4, §5.4, §6.2.3): case build - trunk build --release writes web/dist with index.html, the .wasm and the wasm-bindgen glue; index.html keeps the canvas, the web.* texts and the inline WebGPU check ahead of the wasm, trunk's auto-loader stripped (M0-T7); cases ready and no-webgpu - web/smoke.mjs drives the box's installed Chrome (playwright-core, headless, §6.2.3's flags) against the `web` service launch.py starts over web/dist (M0-T15): `/` reaches srState "ready" within 30 s and srAdapter is logged; `/?no-webgpu=1` shows srState "no-webgpu" and the three web.no_webgpu_* texts exactly; both read Chrome's command line from chrome://version and refuse a run with --no-sandbox (chromiumSandbox on, M0-D17). Each case builds first when web/dist is not fresh against its inputs

capture.desc: the capture harness, first form (contract §3.3, M0-T8): --capture <script> --out <dir> on the box's window route (xvfb-run + llvmpipe on linux-pc, --offscreen-window on win-laptop, R15) writes one PNG per step of the window's size, the two steps' pixels differ (paused vs running), and a valid captions.json in review_page.py's shape, exit 0; an action not built yet, an unknown action and a bad id are each refused with SR-ERROR, exit 4; the build is the tree's own

licences.desc: G-LIC, no copyleft (contract §5.4, R7): `cargo metadata --locked --filter-platform <target>` over the workspace for the native host and for wasm32-unknown-unknown; every package the target resolves to has a licence expression with an alternative made only of §5.4's list (OR, AND, WITH parsed, `/` read as OR; one named exception, epaint_default_fonts, contract §0.5 [M0-T14]); a missing licence or any other is NO-GO naming the package. The parser's own fixed-expression checks run first in each case. `npm ls --all --json` in web/ is case `npm` (M0-T14, added with web/package.json by M0-T15)

watch_only.desc: G-WATCH, labels watch and never drive (contract §1.1, §5.4; M0-T16): a static scan - no file under crates/sr-engine/src/step/ or crates/sr-engine/shaders/ names `observe`, `Stage`, `Tracker` or a §2.11 calibration key other than `physics_hash` (the keys read from the contract's schema line); the log counts the files scanned (≥ 2), an empty folder is NO-GO, a hit names file and line

skip_classes.reason: the harness's own manifest and anchor - a wrong entry shows as a red or an uncovered scope, never graded by one
instruction and config files - no scope grades text; the lead reads them

reports, tasks, the contract and docs - until a scope reads one (the `strings` scope reads the contract's strings block, M0-T13, and takes that file out of this class by its paths), a V block reads them
